subject: DPIA / Art. 28–30: sample evidence & transfer mechanism details
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@novabank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@novabank.com
Date: 2026-02-16T08:14:00Z
Subject: DPIA / evidence request for EU onboarding - initial ask

Hi Vanessa,

As part of Nova Bank's onboarding checklist we're working through the DPIA and vendor due diligence packets. Can you provide a small set (sampling) of the following so our privacy team can validate Art. 28/30 controls and cross-border transfer mechanisms?

Request (sample):
- An excerpt of your Article 30 processing register showing processing purposes, categories of data, and subprocessors for the last 12 months.
- A short statement of transfer mechanisms you rely on for EU->US flows (SCCs, SCC+supplemental measures, onshore options).
- Evidence of KMS/HSM usage for customer key material where applicable and a redacted KMS diagram or description.
- A dataflow diagram focused on account identifiers and access paths for processors/subprocessors.
- Any DPA addendum text you propose for audit/access rights and notification timelines.

We understand some items are sensitive; redaction is acceptable as long as the structure and controls are clear. Our privacy team will review and (if needed) ask for one follow-up sample.

Can we get these by end of day Thursday (2026-02-19)? If there's anything that requires approvals or legal review, let us know and we'll schedule a short call.

Thanks — Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Vendor Privacy, Nova Bank

----
Marta's request is limited to onboarding validation and should not be used for broad audits yet.

Hi Marta —

Thanks for the clear checklist. We can provide a redacted sample set that covers Art. 28/30 structure, transfer mechanisms, and KMS usage by Thu 2026-02-19 EOD. Plan below:

1) Ben will export a 3-month excerpt of the Art. 30 processing register with PII categories and subprocessors redacted to initials.
2) I'll attach a short DPA addendum draft that includes audit rights language and notification timelines.
3) Ben will include a redacted KMS diagram and a brief note on HSM usage and key custody.
4) We'll attach a simplified dataflow diagram focused on account IDs and who can decrypt in production.

We will mark any sensitive hostnames/ARNs as [REDACTED] and provide a separate internal ledger for auditors on request (subject to contract). If Nova Bank needs an inspect-on-site option or dedicated onshore hosting for specific processing, we'll indicate availability and lead times.

Ben and I will prepare the files and share via a secure Drive link; Laura is copied for any legal/managerial approvals.

If you have a preferred format for the register excerpt (CSV vs spreadsheet), tell us and we'll prioritize that.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Marta / Vanessa —

Uploading the requested sample artifacts. Attached in this message are four short stubs:
- redwood_processor_register_excerpt.csv (columns: processing_activity, data_categories, legal_basis, subprocessors) — subprocessors redacted to initials (e.g., "CDN: A.R., Logging: B.C.").
- art30-dataflow-diagram.png (simplified, shows core path: client -> Redwood API -> KV cache -> inference pool; indicates where PII is tokenized).
- dpa-addendum-transfer-mechanisms.docx (proposed addendum text for audit & transfer clauses).
- kms-hsm-note.txt (one-page explanation of KMS model: customer keys are optionally supported via BYOK; production keys stored in HSM-backed KMS; access by SRE on a limited, audited role).

Quick notes on transfer mechanisms:
- For hosted EU customers we offer EU-region deployment; for cross-border flows we rely on the EU SCCs v4 + supplemental technical and organisational measures (encryption-in-transit, per-customer keying, limited access controls, logging & retention controls).
- We can propose an SCC+Annex that maps data categories to subprocessors and control objectives (if Nova needs that mapping, we can deliver as part of the DPA negotiation).
- Onshore options: Dedicated/Private deployments are available if Nova requires no cross-border transfers; estimated provisioning lead time: 6–8 weeks.

Attachments are redacted where appropriate. If your team needs a signed attestation (SOC2-derived controls) we can produce a tailored evidence pack under an executed DPA.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Vanessa / Ben —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround. A couple of legal/controls points before we hand over anything beyond the redacted samples:

- Approvals: For any images or diagrams that show internal hostnames or roles beyond high-level (e.g., individual engineer on-call contacts), redact.
- Audit language: we'll include the DPA addendum but ensure it references a scoped "evidence pack" process and that any onsite review is limited to a defined checklist and notice period.
- SCCs: don't reference draft internal mappings as "final"; mark them as "proposed mapping for negotiation".

Marta — once we upload the redacted bundle to the secure Drive link we'll also provide a short readme that lists what was redacted and why. If Nova wants a follow-up call to walk through the KMS/HSM notes and transfer safeguards, please propose two 30-minute slots and we'll confirm availability.

Laura Bennett
